📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the biggest shopping events of the year is finally here: Black Friday.

Early Black Friday deals started rolling in weeks ago, but now we're well into the official sales. Yes, instead of standing in a cold line at 4 a.m. the day after Thanksgiving, we get to shop online under cozy blankets while watching Christmas movies.

Since the deals between retailers can feel overwhelming, it's good to head into the mega-sale event with a proposal. From knowing when sales from retailers like Amazon and Best Buy start to knowing which products will likely go on sale to preparing your own shopping list, we've got you covered on everything you need to know to shop Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

In a recent development, this year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27, but that date isn't all that important these days. Almost every major retailers has already started official Black Friday sales. We expect to see some special deals drop on Nov. 27, but if you're looking to shop Black Friday sales, it's your time to shine.

Absolutely yes. The mega-retailer's sale kicked off Thursday, Nov. 19 — more info on the full date range of the sale is below. Expect deals on everything from the year's top tech to home essentials. Naturally, Amazon's devices also get markdowns across the board. So far, the retailer has teased the following:.

Save up to 45% on Amazon's 2024 Kindle Colorsoft, 55-inch Ember Artline TV, and 55-inch Ember Mini LED-Series TV.

Save up to 50% on select headphones and speakers from Sony, Beats, JBL, Marshall, and Sonos.

Save up to 40% on select Ninja appliances, including the Creami, Foodi, and Slushi.

Save up to 40% on select iRobot and Bissell floorcare.

Save up to $500 on select Balsam Hill and Fraser Hill Farm artificial Christmas trees.

Amazon: Amazon's Black Friday sale runs from Thursday, Nov. 19 to Nov. 30, offering 12 consecutive days of deals. Each day of the sale will feature "Today's Massive Deals," where select products will be on sale for up to 60% off, except for on Black Friday and Cyber Monday proper. One batch of deals will go live at 3 a.m. ET, while another will go on sale at 11 a.m. ET.

Recent findings suggest that best Buy: Black Friday at Best Buy starts on Nov. 19, and runs through Saturday, Nov. 28. Its Cyber Monday sale runs from Nov. 29 to Nov. 30, with a Cyber Week sale that extends savings from Dec. 1 to Dec. 6. Total and Plus members of the My Best Buy program are also eligible to earn double points on their purchases from Nov. 19 to Dec. 6.

Recent findings suggest that walmart: Walmart has three major sale events throughout November: the early Black Friday sale from Nov. 12 to Nov. 15, the Black Friday sale from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26), and the online-only Cyber Monday sale from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

Sources indicate that target: Target's first Early Black Friday sale kicked off Nov. 5 to Nov. 7. From Nov. 1 to Dec. 24, Target's Deal of the Day offer kicks off, featuring new deals every day. Every weekend after Nov. 7, the retailer will also drop new limited-time holiday offers.

Sources indicate that considering prices went up this year on pretty much Apple devices except for AirPods, Black Friday will be the time to pick up upcoming Apple devices. The short answer: Apple products will absolutely be on sale this Black Friday. The slightly longer answer: the best place to pick up Apple products during Black Friday sales will be at retailers like Amazon, Walmart, or Best Buy, which often duke it out to see who will drop a MacBook or pair of AirPods to the record-low price first (or, more impressively, keep it in stock the longest). Already in the lead-up, MacBooks are $250 off, and the AirPods Pro 3 are $100 off.

As for Apple itself holding Black Friday sales, the Apple Store features its own Black Friday sale every year: a free gift card for future use with the purchase of select devices. We expect to see the same this year, so we recommend picking up your Apple devices elsewhere if you're looking to save as much cash as possible.

Target has great Black Friday deals if you're looking for toys, Lego sets, Christmas decor, books, or small kitchen appliances. Target's Deal of the Day offers extra savings on hot items, and you can preview upcoming deals several days before they happen, giving shoppers time to set a reminder.

Walmart doesn't skimp out on Black Friday deals, and they tend to compete with the best Amazon sales, like $149 Apple AirPods Pro 3. You can also get the Nespresso Vertuo Pop coffee and espresso maker for a rock-bottom price of $59. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Officially, Walmart's Black Friday deals are live through Nov. 29, followed by Cyber Monday from Nov. 30 to Dec. 2. If a deal you were hoping to grab at Amazon sells out, it's always worth checking stock at Walmart.

Best Buy gets in on the sale action, and it's worth paying close attention to the retailer's doorbuster deals which offer ridiculous savings but tend to sell out rapidly (R.I.P $149.99 Ninja Slushi). Like Walmart, Best Buy tends to price-match Amazon deals. If you wind up needing a gift in a hurry, Best Buy tends to offer great in-store pickup options as well as quick shipping.

While Black Friday brings many of the best prices of the year, it's not the end-all, be-all for every product out there. According to Google-analyzed holiday trends, fancy cookware and suitcases hit their lowest prices in late December, while tech like TVs and gaming consoles are likely to hit their lowest prices during Black Friday and Cyber Week (with the latter seeing one final dip right before Christmas).

There can be some variance from category to category, so we recommend keeping track of Mashable's deals coverage. Our team has been covering Black Friday (and deals in general) for nearly a decade, so we can tell your firsthand whether or not a product is worth grabbing during the height of sales.

With Black Friday proper bringing some of the lowest prices, what deals are worth shopping now? It's an especially relevant question in 2026, a year that saw many historic price increases across everything from laptops to Kindles. In other words, shopping smart has never been a smarter decision, which is why we've gathered some of the best early Black Friday savings so far.

According to recent reports, the more apt question is what doesn't go on sale during Black Friday. That's to say, if there's a product you're looking to grab on sale, whether that be a new TV or paper towels, Black Friday is the time to do it.

According to recent reports, beyond the deals we have listed above, we expect to see more savings on MacBooks, Windows laptops, video games and consoles, robot vacuums, regular stick vacuums, drones, trading cards, books, board games, and power tools. This list is by no means exhaustive — if there's a good deal worth writing up, you'll likely find it in our deals coverage.

It has been revealed that the best Black Friday deals generally last through Cyber Monday, which falls on Nov. 30 this year. Some deals do linger through the week, and some Cyber Monday sales (such as Walmart's) are scheduled to extend beyond Cyber Monday proper. And as Target's deal-of-the-day sale demonstrates, there are almost always Black Friday-worthy sales through essentially Christmas. That said, for the best shot at scoring massive savings (and for catching a deal while it's still available), shopping during Black Friday weekend is typically a good rule of thumb.

Amazon and Walmart don't offer any price matching policy. Best Buy's Holiday Price Match Guarantee offers price matches against itself through Jan. 15, 2027 on products purchased from Oct. 30 to Dec. 31. Target used to offer price matching against other retailers during the holidays, but now its policy resembles Best Buy's: Target shoppers who made a purchase on or after Nov. 1 in person or online can request a price match if they spot a drop on or before Dec. 24.

Black Friday (Nov. 27): 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. local time, with ticketing system for high-demand items.

Black Friday (Nov. 27): Stores open at 6 a.m. local time and close at current closing time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft announced this week that its To Do app is shutting down soon, taking the legacy of Wunderlist with it.
  • Industry observers note that microsoft is shutting down its To Do app at the end of June 2027, with focus moving to the newer Planner app.
  • As we bring personal task management into Planner, we will phase out To Do.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft announced this week that its To Do app is shutting down soon, taking the legacy of Wunderlist with it.

Industry observers note that microsoft is shutting down its To Do app at the end of June 2027, with focus moving to the newer Planner app. The company explains:.

As we bring personal task management into Planner, we will phase out To Do. The To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. Connections that other apps use to access To Do tasks will continue beyond that date, and we’ll provide separate notice before those connections are retired. We’re also updating existing task integrations across Microsoft 365 to connect with Planner, so you’ll be able to create or manage tasks in the Microsoft experiences you already use. Although To Do tasks are already visible in Planner, they will not be migrated to the fresh private plan. Customers using personal Microsoft accounts will need to choose another app. Our To Do transition guidance  will help you understand what’s changing and plan your next steps.

Recent findings suggest that to Do was built on the foundation of Wunderlist, a wildly popular to do list app that Microsoft purchased in 2015. Wunderlist later shut down in 2020.

Microsoft’s shuffle, notably, leaves general consumers without a replacement app. To Do was available to anyone with a Microsoft account, where Planner is available only to enterprise/business consumers. So, for long-time Wunderlist users who followed Microsoft migration, this is the end of the road and it’s officially time to move to another app.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This past election, Americans across the country rejected data centers, voting to restrict upcoming projects in their communities.
  • Pollution from data centers is three times higher than previously estimated, according to a new study from the Harvard Data Science Initiative.
  • The study examined 403 "hyperscale" data centers and found that emissions from these facilities were underestimated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This past election, Americans across the country rejected data centers, voting to restrict upcoming projects in their communities. As voters push back against data centers, a new study out of Harvard reveals startling revelations about the severity of the pollution they create.

Pollution from data centers is three times higher than previously estimated, according to a new study from the Harvard Data Science Initiative.

The study examined 403 "hyperscale" data centers and found that emissions from these facilities were underestimated. In fact, the lead author Gianluca Guidi believes that their research only provides a "floor estimate." When factoring in the thousands of data centers across the country, many of which were not included in the study, the energy use is likely much higher.

Recent findings suggest that the study found that the largest data centers in the U.S. use as much energy in a single year as the state of Michigan does. Carbon emissions from these data centers surpassed those of entire countries.

Sources indicate that researchers found that 2 percent of all electricity use in the U.S. during the study period came from data centers. A single data center included in the study consumed as much energy as 30,000 homes on average. Certain U.S. states are worse off than others in terms of climate pollution from data centers, according to Harvard researchers. For example, Virginia has the most data centers, and fossil fuel-burning power plants are most common there. Other states, such as Oregon, have green-friendly, eclectic grids, so data centers residing there are likely emitting less pollution.

Data centers have become a controversial topic across the U.S. Thanks to the AI boom, the tech industry is looking to build more data centers in the U.S. to provide compute for AI models and research. However, data centers are proving unpopular in many communities. Some state legislatures have taken action to restrict data center buildouts and stiffen regulations around the industry. As previously mentioned, 44 ballot measures to restrict data center buildout were passed by voters during the midterm elections.

And the movement against AI data centers appears to only be growing. For example, environmental activist Erin Brockovich introduced her own data center tracking initiative earlier this year.

In a recent development, the tech and AI industries are currently struggling with a series of other complications. However, based on what studies are finding, it seems the anti-data-center movement will continue to be a thorn in the side of major tech and AI.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

The best (and weirdest) Spotify Wrapped features through the years

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every year, Spotify Wrapped kicks off the same ritual: Instagram Stories fill up with top-five lists, friends compare how many minutes they spent listening, and someone has to explain how a song they swear they barely played ended up at No.
  • In a recent development, over the years, Spotify has gotten a lot more creative with those numbers.
  • Recent findings suggest that in 2023, Spotify Wrapped could tell you where in the world people listened to music just like you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every year, Spotify Wrapped kicks off the same ritual: Instagram Stories fill up with top-five lists, friends compare how many minutes they spent listening, and someone has to explain how a song they swear they barely played ended up at No. 1.

In a recent development, over the years, Spotify has gotten a lot more creative with those numbers. It's turned listening habits into personality tests, matched people with cities they've never visited, and even stacked their favorite genres into a sandwich. With another Wrapped around the corner, we're looking back at the features that made us laugh, argue with our results, or wonder what exactly Spotify was thinking.

Recent findings suggest that in 2023, Spotify Wrapped could tell you where in the world people listened to music just like you. The feature, called Sound Town, matched listeners with one of more than 1,300 places, from Provo, Utah, to Cuiabá, Brazil, to Burlington, Vermont. To get a match, at least three of your most-played artists had to be especially popular in the same city.

Sources indicate that the fun was finding out what else people in your Sound Town had on repeat. For example, SZA's "Kill Bill" was No. 1 in both Berkeley, California, and Cambridge, Massachusetts, and came in fifth in Jakarta, Indonesia. In Burlington, Vermont, Noah Kahan had four songs in the top 10. "Stick Season" was No. 1, naturally.

Once people started posting, a few cities, like Berkeley, Burlington, and Cambridge, took on a meaning of their own. Queer listeners comparing results noticed some familiar names in the mix, including boygenius, Charli XCX, and Janelle Monáe.

Spotify got in on it, tagging all three cities in a post, writing, "hey besties.".

Somehow, with this feature, a city you'd never set foot in could suddenly feel like a place where you knew people, even if all you'd shared was a playlist. — Olivia Tauber.

Spotify Wrapped added an aura reading in 2021. For Audio Aura, Spotify worked with aura reader Mystic Michaela to turn the two moods that demonstrated up most in a listener's streaming history into a colorful, shareable card. The more someone listened to music in a particular mood, the darker its shade appeared.

Industry observers note that each color said something about what people reached for when they put on music. Blue was for listeners who wanted to sit with their feelings, orange was for those who needed a confidence boost, and pink was for the hopeless romantics. The cards also spelled out the moods behind the colors, with labels like "blissful" and "chill.".

When Wrapped dropped on Dec. 1, listeners started posting their Audio Auras on Twitter. One user took their "chill and euphoric" result as confirmation that they had excellent taste and were, in fact, the hottest person ever.

By the next day, BuzzFeed had made a quiz predicting your 2022 aura. Later that month, Spotify built full-size pods based on the cards' color combinations for its Wrapped party, where Mystic Michaela gave guests in-person aura readings. Cute! — OT.

One of Spotify's weirdest experiments was a podcast with an audience of one. Built with Google's NotebookLM, the Wrapped AI Podcast turned your listening stats into a conversation between two AI hosts. They addressed you by name, talked through your most-played songs and artists, and guessed what you might have been doing while you listened. After a year of hearing other people talk on Spotify, you could finally listen to an episode about you.

According to recent reports, the guesses were where things got weird. For example, when Gizmodo's Florence Ion tried it at the time, the hosts wondered whether her longest listening day had been a road trip. (She'd actually spent it crying and playing sad music.).

When Wrapped dropped on Dec. 4, some listeners actually complained that Spotify had put too much emphasis on the AI podcast. They missed the human touch of features of past. — OT.

If you've ever taken a personality test and immediately made the results your entire identity, Spotify Wrapped 2022 had something for you. That year, Spotify introduced Your Listening Personality, assigning listeners one of 16 personality types based on their relationship with music.

Much like the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI), Spotify's personality test measured four different characteristics: Familiarity vs. Exploration, Timelessness vs. Newness, Loyalty vs. Variety, and Commonality vs. Uniqueness. Each listener received a four-letter combination and a corresponding personality.

Industry observers note that even the artists got in on it. Charli XCX was classified as a Specialist, which she told Spotify made sense, given that her attention was hard to capture but once it had it, she was committed. (She also revealed that she'd listened to Will Smith's "Miami" roughly 200 times that year.).

The feature arrived at a time when the internet's appetite for personality tests seemed insatiable. Why stop at your zodiac sign, your MBTI, and your Enneagram when you could add a Spotify-assigned personality to your bio? For the record, I'm an ENVC. — Crystal Bell.

Were you in your "Pink Pilates Princess Strut Pop" era or your "Sweater Weather Softcore Indie" era? These were actual things Spotify wanted you to consider in 2024.

Sources indicate that that year, Spotify introduced Your Music Evolution, a feature that divided your year into as many as three distinct musical phases. Spotify considered when your interest in certain artists and genres peaked, how much time you spent listening to them, and how significantly those habits deviated from your usual tastes.

In a recent development, the resulting labels sounded like someone had fed a year's worth of TikTok aesthetics into a musical Mad Libs generator. There was "Surf Crush Beach Reggae" and "Wild West Slow Dance Country," among countless other combinations. April was my "Pumpkin Spice Roller Skating Pop" season, which felt like a personal assault on my taste.

In a year when seemingly everything had become an aesthetic, from the way we dressed to the way we decorated our bedrooms, it felt appropriate that our listening habits got the same treatment.

Industry observers note that were these legitimate musical genres? Not exactly. Did they sound suspiciously like something you'd find on a Pinterest mood board? Absolutely. — CB.

In 2025, Spotify gave listeners a fresh reason to have an existential crisis: their Listening Age. The feature was inspired by a psychological phenomenon known as the reminiscence bump, the idea that people tend to form particularly strong attachments to music from their formative years.

To calculate your Listening Age, Spotify examined the release years of the songs you streamed, identifying a five-year period of music you listened to disproportionately often compared with other people your age. It then assumed you would have been between 16 and 21 when that music came out.

Sources indicate that someone with an affinity for late-'70s music, for example, could receive a Listening Age of 63, regardless of their actual age. Naturally, some people felt called out.

Of course, you don't have to have lived through a particular musical era to feel nostalgic for it. Younger generations regularly discover decades-old songs through TikTok, television soundtracks, and their parents' record collections.

It's easy to see why Listening Age was a hit with people. The opportunity to receive a completely unnecessary personal assessment and immediately make it everyone else's business is part of what makes Spotify Wrapped so irresistible. And there's something particularly funny about a 22-year-old proudly announcing that they have the music taste of a 65-year-old as if it's some kind of cultural flex. — CB.

Remember the peak of the internet's main character era? In 2021, TikTok encouraged us to romanticize our lives, and Spotify gave us the soundtrack to do it.

According to recent reports, with 2021: The Movie, Spotify assigned some of your most-played songs to scenes in a fictional movie starring you. There was a song for your opening credits, a dramatic declaration of love, a showdown with a rival dance crew, and even a battle against a supernatural villain. In my 2021 Wrapped, my opening credits were soundtracked by Rosé's "On The Ground," which suggests my movie was less of a rom-com and more of an existential coming-of-age drama.

It has been revealed that what made this feature so charming was how it leaned into something music lovers already did: imagine elaborate cinematic scenarios while listening to their favorite songs. Anyone who's ever stared wistfully out of a train window with their headphones on knows exactly what I'm talking about.

Recent findings suggest that spotify understood the assignment with this one. Bring it back! — CB.

Of all the ways Spotify could have visualized your top five music genres, it chose lunch.

Industry observers note that in 2023, Spotify Wrapped served up a personalized genre sandwich, with each of your five most-listened-to genres represented by a colorful layer between two pieces of bread. The thickness of each layer reflected how much you listened to that genre relative to the others.

Recent findings suggest that according to Spotify's global marketing team, the sandwich was chosen because it was globally recognizable and easily customizable. There were even different types of bread.

Spotify committed to the bit, too. The manufacturer teamed up with viral Brooklyn deli owner Rahim Mohamed, better known online as General Ock, to make an actual sandwich inspired by New York City's five most-streamed genres that year: pop, hip-hop, rock, indie, and Latin.

Was a sandwich the most intuitive way to visualize a year's worth of listening data? Probably not. But there was something delightfully absurd about telling your friends that your music taste consisted of a thick slab of K-pop, a generous helping of indie rock, and a thin slice of emo.

Sources indicate that personally, I'd like to know what sauce pairs best with existential synth-pop. — CB.

It has been revealed that crystal Bell is the Digital Culture Editor at Mashable, where she leads coverage of the creator economy, internet culture, and digital life. Her work focuses on the people, platforms, and communities shaping modern entertainment, from YouTube creators and livestreamers to fandoms, social media trends, and the evolving relationship between technology and culture. She also oversees the Mashable 101, the publication's annual list recognizing the internet's most influential creators.

Industry observers note that previously, she was the entertainment director at MTV News, where she helped expand the brand's coverage of fan culture, K-pop, and the internet's most passionate communities. Her work has appeared in Teen Vogue, Rolling Stone, PAPER, NYLON, ELLE, Glamour, NME, W, The FADER, and elsewhere on the internet.

Recent findings suggest that she's exceptionally fluent in fandom and will gladly make you a K-pop playlist and/or provide anime recommendations upon request. Crystal lives in Newly introduced York City with her two black cats, Howl and Sophie.

Olivia Tauber is the deputy editor of digital culture, covering creators, media, movies, beauty, and more. Based in New York, her work has appeared in The New York Times, Vanity Fair, The Cut, Teen Vogue, Complex, and Interview Magazine. She holds a Master's degree in Journalism from NYU and a Bachelor's from the University of Michigan. She also runs Fan Mail, a weekly pop-culture newsletter.

According to recent reports, this comes after a report came out last month indicating Samsung cut production of its Galaxy A devices by “approximately 20%.” Memory makes up more of the overall component cost in mid-range devices. So the cost of the overall device is more influenced by memory prices than in a flagship, like the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Even with a specced-out build, there’s more dispersion of costly components, rather than one expensive component like memory taking up the bulk of the production price.

That cut is estimated to be around 10 million units, and this latest report only furthers the claim that mid-range devices are too costly to make for Samsung.

The opposite is true for the Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra, which reportedly got the green light for increased production prior to launch. Price suggestions average an increase of $200 for the Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27 Plus. As for the high-spec Galaxy S27 Pro and Ultra, they start at $1,399 and $1,499, respectively.

There was already a massive disparity between those devices and the increasingly validated Galaxy A devices, and the gap is shrinking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the fact that Moto Tag 2 has only been on the market for a few months at this point, Motorola is apparently getting Moto Tag 3 out in the not-too-distant future, and it’s already on sale (probably by mistake).

Sources indicate that an Amazon UK listing went up this week for “Moto Tag 3,” a newly introduced version of Motorola’s Android Find Hub tracker. The listing shows the tracker in “Pantone Lucent White,” while a second image shared by Evan Blass shows the new model in a vibrant purple color.

There’s no indication of major changes in “Moto Tag 3,” with Motorola still claiming similar battery life, using a CR2032 battery, and supporting UWB in Android Find Hub.

The listing (thanks Matt!) explains:.

Motorola moto tag 3 helps you locate everyday items with precision and reliability. Using Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth technology, it works with the Android Find Hub network to track belongings both nearby and at distance. With more than 500 days of battery life powered by a replaceable CR2032 battery, it is designed for long-term use. Built-in privacy protections, encrypted location data, and unwanted tracking alerts support secure tracking in a compact, IP68-rated design suitable for daily carry.

In a recent development, “Moto Tag 3” is on sale from Amazon UK, though it comes with a “1-4 month” shipping estimate. This is almost certainly a slip-up, especially given the timing.

This comes much earlier than expected. The original Moto Tag released in 2024, with its sequel being revealed in early 2026 before going on sale in the US less than six months ago in June 2026. Such an early move to “Moto Tag 3” is interesting, to say the least, so we’ll have to wait and see if there are any changes in tow beyond just the latest colors. That remarked, these are really nice colors. It’s also possible this is just the same model with a slip-up in branding – the model number on the Amazon listing is unchanged.

We’ll have to wait and see what happens. Moto Tag 2 did debut at CES in January, and with Razr Flex also in the works, Motorola almost certainly would launch an updated tracker at the trade show if it truly does plan to do so soon.

This comes right as Moto Tag 2 has hit its lowest price ever at just $18.99 amid Black Friday sales.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Samsung came in at 25%, up 1% from last year (likely driven by a very successful Fold 8 launch during Q3), while Motorola shrank from 12% to 8%.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest quarterly data for the US smartphone market reveals that Google Pixel is holding its ground despite the overall market faltering, and the other two major Android brands struggling.

The top smartphone brands in the United States include Apple, Samsung, Motorola, and Google Pixel in that order. Apple continues to absolutely dominate at a whopping 57% market share in Q3 2026, up from 50% during the same period last year.

Samsung came in at 25%, up 1% from last year (likely driven by a very successful Fold 8 launch during Q3), while Motorola shrank from 12% to 8%.

Google Pixel made up 6%, down 1% from Q3 2025, Counterpoint Research highlights. Q3 is important for Google as it includes the company’s new August release window for new flagships. It’s not surprising that Google dropped a percentage point year-over-year, as the company’s Pixel 11 launch was not particularly exciting, especially as prices rose over the previous generation. If anything, only dropping 1% must be pretty encouraging given the overall market conditions and RAMageddon of it all.

Something to note – Google Pixel is technically growing this year compared to last. Just out of view on this latest upgrade, Q2 2026 saw Google’s share up 1% year-over-year, and Q1 was also up compared to the same period in 2025. Counterpoint previously mentioned that the Pixel brand “remains aggressive in postpaid” carriers, but notes that Pixel 11 shipments were “weaker YoY.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It feels like tech everywhere is getting more and more expensive, but the Black Friday sales give you the opportunity to secure some rare bargains. If you're looking for a tablet and have a budget of just £100, then your options are usually extremely limited: entry-level models like the Lenovo Tab One or the Samsung Galaxy Tab A11 often go for more than £150.

According to recent reports, luckily, Amazon has come to the rescue with its brand-fresh Alexa Tablet line, which has seen a huge swathe of discounts in the ongoing early Black Friday sales. The cheapest option is the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8, the brand's entry-level model, which has plummeted to just £99.99 from £199.99 thanks to a massive 50% price cut.

Although the specs are modest, you're still getting a fully functional, working tablet for under £100, and in 2026 that's worth shouting about. The low price makes this a fantastic pick if you're shopping for kids, as you won't need to worry about them damaging something that will cost a huge amount to replace.

Despite the low cost, there are some premium elements to the design too. The case is a durable aluminium rather than plastic, and the chipset powering it all is the same MediaTek 8-Core processor found in the much pricier Alexa Tablet 11 and is capable of delivering reliable day-to-day performance.

Amazon's most basic Android tablet is a great little budget buy at under £100. The octa-core MediaTek SoC is perfect for most basic use cases, though the 64GB of storage and modest 4GB of RAM could be limitations if you intend to download a lot of apps or multitask often. Also be aware that this model comes with lock-screen ads by default, but you can at least pay a small fee to remove them.

Key specs at a glance: Display - 1340x800 60Hz LCD, RAM - 4GB, Storage - 64GB, SoC - octa-core MediaTek, MicroSD card slot - No.

Industry observers note that ✅Recommended if: you want a bargain-basement, compact tablet for basic day-to-day use or to give to the kids. With its modest specs, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 isn't going to be a good fit for power owners – but if you just want to browse the web, respond to emails, read e-books, or watch movies via streaming, it will more than suffice.

The octa-core SoC and robust aluminium case also mean that it's better than some more expensive competitors in certain regards.

Sources indicate that ❌Skip this deal if: you require more storage or RAM, or want a better screen. The substantial limitations here are that it has 64GB of storage and 4GB of RAM. The storage unfortunately cannot be upgraded, as there is no microSD card slot, so you will likely run out of space rapidly if you want to download Android apps. The RAM will also limit your ability to multitask.

Finally, the screen is just 1340x800 resolution – HD but not Full HD. It won't be too noticeable given the small 8.7-inch size, but might look a bit fuzzy to those with sharp eyes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Garmin and Bark are competing for your money this year, and these sales make it easy to get something fun that’ll keep your kids safe and in touch.

Industry observers note that many parents struggle with the idea of getting a smartphone for their kids. If you want your kids to stay in touch but not have access to all the garbage on the internet, a smartwatch is the best alternative. I’ve tested a lot of kids’ smartwatches over the years, and I can easily recommend the two in the picture above: the Bark Watch and the Garmin Bounce 2.

Industry observers note that both watches are on sale well ahead of Black Friday, too! The Bark Watch is $11 off at Amazon ($274 total) and $50 off at Bark, while the Garmin Bounce 2 is $50-$64 off (starting at $235) depending on the color you choose. The least expensive Garmin Bounce 2 is the blue color in the photo I took above, which my son loved.

It has been revealed that choosing between the two is easy enough. Garmin’s watch is the least complicated and comes in a slightly more durable case with fun colors. It’s slightly cheaper than Bark, but doesn’t have any health sensors on board. It mainly tracks steps, allows your kids to message or call you, and gives you geofencing and location tracking through a $9.99 per month LTE subscription blueprint. It’s got a 5ATM rating and a polycarbonate case, so it’s quite durable.

Sources indicate that the Garmin Bounce 2 is preloaded with a few mini games and educational apps, plus the Garmin Jr. app has built-in unlockables and rewards parents can set for doing chores, completing schoolwork, etc. Battery life is roughly 2 days with normal use, but can be less if you’re in an area with poor LTE reception. The Garmin Bounce 2 is best for kids 10 and under.

The Bark Watch uses Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 hardware and a custom version of Wear OS. It’s a much more powerful watch and only gets a day of battery life because of it. This one feels like a midpoint between a kids’ watch and a standard Wear OS watch, as it has all the power of Wear OS but doesn’t feature the Google Play Store. It doesn’t have any games, social media, or browsers.

Recent findings suggest that since it uses Samsung’s hardware, it includes cutting-edge health sensors that your kids can use, plus great multitasking and a svelte, attractive design. Bark charges $15 per month for its plan, which includes a Bark App subscription for the whole family. I also use the Bark App on my son’s phone, which helps me monitor his usage and make sure he’s safe online. The extra $5 per month adds up, but it’s absolutely worth it if you want to add the Bark App to another phone or tablet.

Recent findings suggest that the Bark Watch is fine enough for younger kids, but the design and lack of games feel more like an “older kids’ watch” to me, and my 12-year-old son agrees. Either way you go, these are fantastic choices that you’ll be happy with, especially with a nice little deal.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile.
  • If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you picked up a fresh iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

If someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

It has been revealed that the ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually indicates every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

It has been revealed that both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR claims it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

Sources indicate that both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

According to recent reports, the same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Industry observers note that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

Sources indicate that A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

According to recent reports, why it matters: ESR notes the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Sources indicate that installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

It has been revealed that holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. An extra USB-C port lets a second device charge simultaneously. 9to5Mac’s Michael Burkhardt went hands-on with the Xtend 45W earlier this month and noted it’s an excellent iPhone fast charger on the go.

According to recent reports, it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR indicates it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

In a recent development, ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

Recent findings suggest that for a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

According to recent reports, the trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR says the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

Industry observers note that the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Both cases also have 260g of magnetic strength, so they snap onto MagSafe chargers, Apple Watch chargers, and MagSafe batteries if you need to charge your AirPods. Again, it’s extremely strong, but extremely easy to unlock with one hand.

The ESR Cyber FlickLock Magnetic Case is extremely durable and has a clip hook, so you can hang your AirPods on a backpack while hiking or cycling. The ESR Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Case brings the same lock in a range of vibrant colors with a carrying lanyard, so you can wear your AirPods on your wrist or attach them to a bag. Both cases come in versions for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2 and 1, and AirPods 5 and 4. No matter which AirPods you or your loved one have, this is the case everyone will love.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

Recent findings suggest that the ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. It fits 44mm, 45mm, 46mm, and 49mm models across Apple Watch Ultra 1 through 4, Series 4 through 12, and SE 1 through 3, and it comes in several colors to match your outfit or your mood that day.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Equinox Watch Band is 20% off.

The best gifts are the ones that get used every day, and accessories are the part of the Apple experience people live with the most. A case that props up a foldable, a screen protector made with Corning glass, a charger with a built-in cable, and an AirPods case that stays closed even when dropped check all the boxes. ESR truly makes something for everyone and is one of the most trusted names in the Apple accessories ecosystem.

In a recent development, ESR built its Black Friday lineup around the whole Apple ecosystem, from the new iPhone Duo to iPad, AirPods, and even a great Apple Watch band, with premium materials and versatile designs that are durable, functional, and great-looking. ESR’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals run on Amazon from November 19 through November 30 (the Xtend 45W runs through December 1), with discounts of up to 37%!

Be sure to follow ESR on X and Facebook to keep up with all of its latest products, deals, and more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Smartphones and social media have completely changed the way youngsters communicate and interact with each other, but one tech tech giant wants to resurrect a classic method of communication so kids can chat with each other just like the good old days.

Sources indicate that seattle-based brand Tin Can has been reinventing the landline phone for the younger generation for the past two years, and now the kid-friendly mobile devices are finally making their UK debut on November 30, mimicking the design and feel of landline devices that are now a thing of the past. But these aren't fake Fisher-Price toys — these things actually work.

According to recent reports, vibrant and bold in design, Tin Can phones are wired to ensure your child has access to a safer means of communication. Each Tin Can device is Wi-Fi enabled, deliberately leaving screens and algorithms behind for a basic, simplified experience. If you're a parent of a child who's been begging for a smartphone, Tin Can adds a layer of reassurance that your kid is using tech that's safe and foolproof.

Each Tin Can phone operates over a private network, and only contacts approved by adults can call the device, and vice versa. Parents can approve contacts through the Tin Can companion app, where they can also set quiet hours for studying and winding down time. But the safety aspect is just one factor behind Tin Can's development.

Yes, shielding young users from the dangers of digital malice in the age of social media is important, but the brains behind the Tin Can brand want to promote real conversations and independence for its young users. Stripping the device of screens, games, texting, and other means of distraction puts the focus on meaningful communication.

In a recent development, despite the simplicity of Tin Can, you might find its pricing a little more complex. Each Tin Can phone is priced at £100, which, given its simple features, can be a little steep for some. That remarked, your child can contact other Tin Can customers for free on the Can 2 Can plan, which also includes calls to emergency services and calls to Tin Can users in other countries, including the US, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

If you want to access wider communications, you'll need a Party Line plan membership (£8.99 a month or £89.99 a year), where kids can call outside UK numbers with adult approval.

Industry observers note that UK pre-orders for Tin Can started in May this year, and are set to start shipping on November 30. If you want to score one in time for Christmas, Tin Can recommends ordering by December 3 for standard Christmas delivery, or by 10 December with express shipping.

I honestly can't fathom how could Google come out with such poor implementation.

I don't particularly like this one from Samsung, but it surely is 1000000 times better from a UX perspective.

What do you think of Samsung’s alleged Dynamic Island clone? Personally, I’m on board as long as it proves useful, and it seems to be on the right track compared to most other copycats.

  • The biggest shopping day of the year in the United States can also be one of the most precarious, thanks to an increased reliance on e-commerce in the age of rampant cyberattacks and system outages.
  • Here are some common-sense things you can do to make sure Black Friday doesn't become a massive headache for you or your family.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With Black Friday almost upon us, it's time to talk about something other than what you should buy or how much it costs.

The biggest shopping day of the year in the United States can also be one of the most precarious, thanks to an increased reliance on e-commerce in the age of rampant cyberattacks and system outages. There's only so much that you, as an individual shopper, can do to protect yourself if an online retailer is compromised or if you're targeted by a scam artist, but it's notable to understand those measures regardless.

Here are some common-sense things you can do to make sure Black Friday doesn't become a massive headache for you or your family.

One of the main ways that bad actors will try to get you during this holiday shopping season is through phishing, which describes a variety of techniques used by scammers to trick people into giving up money or personal information.

Recent findings suggest that for example, you may get text messages or emails warning of an urgent problem, such as someone using your card to buy something fraudulently, or something more mundane like a delivery notification. While you don't want to outright ignore these warnings because there is always a slim possibility that they are real, you need to double and triple-check things like the sender's email address or a URL or phone number they've given you to solve the "problem." Email phishing requests tend to come from odd-looking, non-standard email addresses, or ones that are misspelled in some way. The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sources indicate that generally speaking, companies will not reach out to you over text or email urgently asking for payment or personal information. If you encounter something like this, you can swiftly run a Google search of the number, address, or the nature of the request, and you'll potentially find other people warning against the phishing scam. Above all else, exercise as much caution as possible and, if needed, reach out directly to the firm in question if you need to verify a request of some sort.

According to recent reports, retailer websites usually give owners the ability to make an account or otherwise save payment and shipping information to make the checkout process more straightforward. You can do this if you want, but given the number of cyberattacks against retailers, doing so puts your information at risk of being compromised.

There is no perfect solution because no form of online payment is 100 percent free from danger. However, using services like Apple Pay or even PayPal can allay the risk a little bit, especially if you use secure multi-factor authentication for those services. In fact, you should use MFA and strong, unique passwords for every account you need to have. It's even better to use a good password manager, which can come up with strong passwords for you that you don't even need to remember.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, sometimes around Black Friday, you'll see deals that seem incredibly generous. Maybe an 80-inch OLED TV is going for $150, or a TikTok account is promising the Nintendo Switch 2 for under $100. In these cases, it's best to understand that you might be getting taken for a ride. Black Friday deals aren't that good, unfortunately.

Sadly, there's no hard-and-fast rule to follow here, other than "be wary of anything that seems too good to be true." That's especially true if the deal is coming from a website or service you've never heard of before. It's one thing to see screaming good deals on slightly more trustworthy platforms like Amazon, but another thing entirely if the retailer in question is obscure or sketchy.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

Industry observers note that proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

Sources indicate that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

If that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to upgrade all your other accounts.

It’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, monkey D. Luffy is once again at the scene of the internet's latest viral meme. Well, technically, it's Twitch streamer Jynxzi playing as the beloved One Piece protagonist in Fortnite, but the distinction hardly matters when you're watching the aspiring King of the Pirates repeatedly fail to obtain a pirate token.

Sometimes, the funniest thing you can do on the internet is fail spectacularly. Or, in Jynxzi's case, come agonizingly close to succeeding.

If you've spent any time scrolling through TikTok or Instagram Reels lately, you've probably heard his now-viral refrain: "Ahh, almost, almost." What began as a moment of frustration on Twitch has since become the internet's go-to response to everything from missed basketball shots to the everyday indignities of being alive.

Here's what you need to know about the "ahh almost almost" meme and how it escaped the confines of Twitch.

In a recent development, the voice behind the meme belongs to Jynxzi, a popular Twitch streamer known for his animated reactions and exaggerated competitive spirit. With 11.8 million followers on Twitch, Jynxzi regularly streams games like Rainbow Six Siege, League of Legends, and Fortnite, often collaborating with other streamers like iShowSpeed and StableRonaldo.

It has been revealed that the meme appears to have originated from a Fortnite livestream in early November, during which Jynxzi repeatedly tried (and failed) to obtain an in-game pirate token. Adding to the comedic effect was his declaration that he was putting in the work while everyone else was out partying. Despite his apparent dedication, success continued to elude him.

Clips of the stream began circulating on TikTok in early November, and it didn't take long for the audio to take on a life of its own outside of the gaming community.

At its most basic, the meme is a reaction to a near miss. But part of what makes it so funny is the gap between how much confidence and effort someone brings to a task and how little they have to show for it. Sometimes, the person in question isn't even remotely close to succeeding, which makes Jynxzi's insistence that he's "almost" there all the more amusing.

Industry observers note that one popular iteration of the trend pokes fun at hustle culture. Videos begin with someone ostensibly working toward a goal, accompanied by the caption "while they're out partying btw," before cutting to footage of them failing at the very thing they've been practicing.

It has been revealed that on TikTok, students document their study sessions only to reveal their failing test grades, a skier attempts a jump and loses their skis in the process, and even a snow leopard fails to catch a mountain goat. In one particularly relatable example, a student sits down to study only to get distracted by K-pop fancams. (We've all been there. Or at least I have.).

It has been revealed that naturally, the meme has found a particularly receptive audience among sports fans. Even NBA teams like the Orlando Magic and the Denver Nuggets have gotten in on the joke.

Think of it as the antithesis of a motivational edit. Instead of rewarding all that hard work with a triumphant moment of personal achievement, the meme celebrates the much more relatable experience of falling short.

You don't necessarily need to know who Jynxzi is to appreciate the joke, either. Much like other bits of streamer vernacular that have made their way into the wider internet lexicon (hey, chat), "almost almost" works just as well as a standalone reaction.

Industry observers note that sometimes, the grind simply doesn't pay off. But at least the memes do.

As for the cameras, the OSTA O1 Pro has a 200MP main shooter paired with a 50MP telephoto lens. There doesn't seem to be a dedicated ultra-wide or macro lens present. There is, however, a 50MP selfie camera on the front of the phone.

Sources indicate that the OSTA O1 Pro is available in three colours: Starry Night Black, Nebula White, and Starlight Purple (though the latter is only offered in 16GB+512GB and 16GB+1TB configurations). Prices start at 5699 CNY for the most basic model, which comes to roughly $855 or £650.

It has been revealed that the OSTA O1 Pro would be a pretty unexceptional mid-range phone, were it not for that unique wide-screen format. It almost looks like an iPhone Air, but fatter and more... compressed. That's not a bad thing either, as I think wider formats like this definitely have a place.

According to recent reports, the popularity of the Samsung Galaxy Fold 8 (which is similarly stout) shows that Android owners are certainly interested in trying form factors that are a bit more out there than the usual candy bar shape. The design of the OSTA O1 Pro also just looks like it would be very comfortable in the hands and fit comfortably in most pockets.

Wider aspect ratios have advantages when it comes to multitasking too, as they make it easier to view multiple windows side by side when using the phone horizontally.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

The major question is whether the OSTA O1 Pro will make it to the West in any official capacity and, sadly, I don't think it's likely. Huawei pulled out of the US market following a US government ban in 2022 and has largely stopped selling its handsets in the UK as well. The only phones at the moment listed on the Huawei UK site are the Mate XT Ultimate Design and Mate X6 foldable, neither of which is actually available to buy on the store.

That remarked, we might still see other manufacturers come out with their own wide-screen model – especially if the OSTA O1 Pro proves popular with Chinese consumers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A short video can make it from TikTok to Instagram Reels to the group chat before lunch.
  • Recent findings suggest that on Wednesday, Nov.
  • Industry observers note that X states video is already its fastest-growing format.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A short video can make it from TikTok to Instagram Reels to the group chat before lunch. X wants more of those clips to land in its feed, too, and it's giving some creators a reason to post videos they've already made.

Recent findings suggest that on Wednesday, Nov. 25, X laid out its intends to get more creators making, sharing, and earning money from videos on the platform. It revealed off an upgraded editor that lets creators record, crop, and caption videos without leaving X, confirmed that its clipping tool is now available on the web, and highlighted an invite-only bonus it's been testing since October for creators who regularly post short, vertical videos.

Industry observers note that X states video is already its fastest-growing format. "Posts with video get 5x the reach and engagement, and 36% of all impressions now go to video," the company’s creator team wrote on Nov. 20.

The editor lets creators record in segments, use a green screen, or turn horizontal footage into a vertical clip with one tap. They can also trim the footage, generate captions, add text, and pick a thumbnail before posting. A separate update, declared Nov. 20, lets creators mix up to 20 photos and videos in a single swipeable post. Those tools join React with Video, which X introduced over the summer to let people respond on camera with the original post behind them.

X is also paying some creators to try vertical video through its Video Kickstart Bonus, an invite-only pilot it began testing in October. To earn the bonus, creators must post 15 qualifying videos on 15 different days within about a month. Each video must be their own work, in a vertical 9:16 format, and under three minutes. A TikTok, Reel, or YouTube Short can count as long as it’s free of another platform’s branding. Creators can see their bonus amount in Creator Studio, X's dashboard for creator tools and payouts. Participants who don’t already have Premium+ also get a free year.

According to recent reports, original Content Rewards also gives creators a way to earn when someone else shares a moment from their video. X's clipping tool, now available on the web as well as iOS and Android, lets users pull an excerpt, add their take, and post it with a link back to the original. Both the person who made the video and the person who posted the clip can earn if they're enrolled in the program.

As X creator product lead Allegra Jacchia put it Wednesday, the goal is to make sure that "when someone clips their video, they get the credit and a share of the earnings.".

Sources indicate that X first rolled out clipping on iOS and Android earlier this month, and Wednesday's announcement confirmed it’s now available on the web, too. To make a clip, open the repost menu on an eligible prerecorded video and select "Clip video." From there, you can trim the footage to between five and 60 seconds and add your commentary before posting. The original video must run for at least two minutes, and the clip can take up no more than 30 percent of it. (So if you're clipping a two-minute video, you get up to 36 seconds.).

Sources indicate that the clip plays right in the feed. For everyone in the replies asking for the full video, there's a shortcut. Tap the "Clip from" label and X takes you straight to the moment in the original video where the excerpt starts. For creators enrolled in Original Content Rewards, earnings from clips show up in their regular payouts.

The video tools will feel familiar to anyone who's spent time on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube Shorts. Letting creators earn a bonus for videos they've already made gives them a reason to add X to the list of places they post.

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mashable ↗ Open Full Page

FCC clears SpaceX to put up to 1 million AI satellites in orbit

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (952 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An AI chatbot may be able to answer a question in seconds, but the chips doing the work need a steady supply of electricity and a way to get rid of all the heat they generate.
  • 25, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) gave Elon Musk's SpaceX conditional approval to deploy up to 1 million satellites for its Starmind project, a network of orbital data centers that would process information for use back on Earth.
  • Recent findings suggest that spaceX says the factory it’s building in Bastrop, Texas, could start turning out satellites for launch as early as late 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An AI chatbot may be able to answer a question in seconds, but the chips doing the work need a steady supply of electricity and a way to get rid of all the heat they generate. SpaceX wants to put some of those chips on satellites and power them with sunlight. In outer space.

On Wednesday, Nov. 25, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) gave Elon Musk's SpaceX conditional approval to deploy up to 1 million satellites for its Starmind project, a network of orbital data centers that would process information for use back on Earth. According to the FCC, it's "the first authorization in U.S. history for a constellation of data centers in space.".

Recent findings suggest that spaceX says the factory it’s building in Bastrop, Texas, could start turning out satellites for launch as early as late 2027. The FCC's deadline for the first one is Nov. 25, 2033. By then, SpaceX has to have a Starmind satellite in its assigned orbit and running.

Two years later, the FCC expects 100,000 satellites to be operating. That's nearly nine times as many satellites as SpaceX's Starlink network has in orbit today. The next deadlines are 500,000 by Nov. 2038 and the full million by Nov. 2040. Under the terms of the order, missing those deadlines would void the authorization.

SpaceX is counting on its Starship rocket to carry the heavy satellites into orbit in large numbers. Amazon Leo, which is building a rival to Starlink, called the proposal a "lofty ambition rather than a real blueprint" in a March petition. Amazon argued it could take SpaceX centuries to put a million satellites in orbit. The FCC rejected Amazon's petition, along with separate challenges from Viasat and the American Astronomical Society.

SpaceX wants the satellites themselves to do the computing. Each one would carry AI chips, solar panels to power them, and radiators to release the heat the chips generate. In some orbits, the panels could collect sunlight nearly around the clock. The satellites would use lasers to pass data between one another and send results back to Earth through Starlink.

Recent findings suggest that in August (pre-Jensen Huang drama), Nvidia mentioned SpaceX intends to adapt its Vera Rubin computing system for the first generation of satellites, "bringing the first CPU built for AI agents to one of the world’s most ambitious AI deployments." (CPU stands for central processing unit.) The best tech deal this week The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile Products available for purchase through affiliate links. If you buy something through links on our site, Mashable may earn an affiliate commission.

The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

Sources indicate that one of the questions for any data center in space is how well its chips will hold up over time. Google is testing that with Project Suncatcher, a prototype satellite that introduced on a SpaceX rocket in October. The chip has already run an AI model in orbit and sent back a haiku about being in space. ("Blue marble below, Data streams in silent grace, Starlight feeds my core.") Google is now testing how the hardware handles radiation and temperature swings.

The same sunlight that would power the satellites could also make them visible from the ground.

Recent findings suggest that the American Astronomical Society said its preliminary simulations suggest that, if SpaceX deploys the full million, tens of thousands could be visible to the naked eye around the world. Reflected sunlight could also leave bright streaks in telescope images and make faint objects harder to see. How much the sky actually changes would depend on details like the satellites' size, materials, and orbits.

Recent findings suggest that the FCC said SpaceX's commitment to work with the National Science Foundation was enough to address the optical astronomy concerns raised in the proceeding. But Starlink has already left its mark on telescope images. At California's Zwicky Transient Facility, for example, researchers found Starlink streaks in 18 percent of images taken at twilight in Aug. 2021, up from less than half a percent in late 2019. A separate study published this year found that several newer Starlink designs were typically dimmer than the originals but still brighter than the goal SpaceX agreed to work toward.

It has been revealed that there's also the question of what happens when the satellites are done working. Under current FCC rules, satellites at those altitudes have to come back through Earth's atmosphere at the end of their missions. SpaceX asked for the option to move some retired satellites into other orbits, including around the sun. The FCC put that request on hold and indicates SpaceX has to submit a final plan for limiting space debris before deploying any Starmind satellites that would operate above 600 kilometers (or about 373 miles).

If Starmind reaches the scale SpaceX has in mind, getting satellites out of orbit safely will be as much a part of running the network as getting them up there. And the launch schedule alone is a tall order. Even if SpaceX gets half a million satellites running by Nov. 2038, it would have just two years to get another half million into orbit and operational. Luckily, that's not my job.

#3034. Can AI make Thanksgiving less painful?
